Return the next passage of fiction.

I offer to carry the empty plates back to the kitchen, without offering to take over anybody's work.

item.text:
You set down your fork.

“I can carry the empty plates through.”

Jo looks over the table. “Thank you. Put them on the counter left of the sink. Leave the pans where they are.”

Nell lifts her envelope out of the way while you gather the first stack. Martin and Rosa have left their plates side by side; Dev’s has a fallen piece of crust near the rim. The crockery is heavier than it looks, thick white cafe ware from one of the opened cartons.

The kitchen is narrow and warmer than the foyer. Shelves hold labelled jars and sealed tubs of dry goods. Owen stands beside the deep sink, sorting the cutlery into a grey tray.

“Here’s clear,” he says, moving the tray aside.

You put down the plates and return for the rest. Jo carries the covered pie herself and sets it beside the remaining stew.

“I’m labelling this, then I’m done for tonight,” she says. “Owen, rubbish can go out through the yard.”

“I’ll take it.”

Nell checks the foyer clock. “I’ll stay until Rosa and Martin finish at seven-forty. Dev’s coming down before he leaves, and I’ll lock the front after that.”

Jo nods. “I’ll be out before then.”

On your second trip, Owen has begun filling the sink. You set the last plates on the counter without touching the pans or the cutlery tray.

“That’s everything,” Jo says. “Thanks, Rowan.”

Behind the auditorium doors, Martin starts the same account for a third time. This version begins with a different year. Rosa lets him finish before asking him to spell June Mercer’s surname.
